newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall on profit-taking by lunch break.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall on profit-taking by lunch break.

text.p: Thai stocks declined slightly in moderate trade by the lunch break on Wednesday as investors sold large capitalised stocks while banks and finance firms reported poor half-year earnings results, brokers said.

"Investors sold as they found there was no positive news to boost the market. Liquidity in the money market is a bit tight today while earnings results of finance companies which are mostly poor didn't have much impact on the market as they were discounted by most investors," said a broker at Securities One.
The index fell 5.70 points to 654.08 on 3.5 billion baht turnover by lunch.

Tight liquidity was another factor in the market as the baht fell to a record low of 31.60 baht per dollar in the domestic market on Wednesday morning on strong commercial demand for dollars, dealers said.
"Foreigners weren't active this morning. I believe they would opt for short-term investment presently due to the absence of positive news," the broker said.
Most of the key sectors declined by the break. The finance sector was first-ranked in terms of value, rising 1.30 percent.
Nava Finance topped the active list, gaining 1.75 baht to 29.75. TelecomAsia shed 0.50 to 41.75.
